locations.name: El Patio de Glòria
locations.description: Lemon-tree patio inside a restored 16th-century manor on Carrer de Sant Jaume — a THREE-minute walk from the Palma Riad. Manus's 'tired and romantic with almost no effort' pick, and the menu reads like Chelsea's order sheet: tuna, scallops, octopus, cod, turbot, seafood rice, vegetable fideuà, pumpkin ravioli. Sunday dinner 19:00–22:30. No sea view — a beautiful enclosed patio instead — which after a full Purobeach day may be exactly right.

locations.name: Ca n'Eduardo
locations.description: 80-year-old seafood institution sitting directly above the fish auction at Palma's fishing pier — the catch comes upstairs from the boats below. Rooftop terrace looks across the harbor to the cathedral. Order the lobster paella or whatever the lonja landed. Kitchen runs continuously 1–10 PM, so it works for an early dinner; a 15-minute seafront walk from the Palma Riad — the only view-dinner in Palma that needs no taxi. Manus's executive pick for the Sep 6 Sunday dinner: verified Sunday service with the kitchen continuous to 10 PM, a verified 13-minute walk from the Riad, and the advice to book 8:30–8:45 PM requesting an exterior table facing the fishing harbor and Cathedral. Chelsea-flexible beyond seafood too: cod, shellfish and vegetable paellas plus a free-range-chicken rice.
locations.address: Carrer Contramuelle Mollet, 3, 07012 Palma, Illes Balears, Spain

references.source: Manus (Sunday dinner with a view report)
references.note: Executive recommendation for Sunday Sep 6: reserve 8:30/8:45 PM, request exterior table facing harbor + Cathedral; Sunday kitchen continuous to 22:00; 13-min walk verified. Menu incl. cod/shellfish/vegetable paellas and free-range-chicken rice.

locations.name: Forn de Sant Joan
locations.description: Traditional Spanish restaurant in central Palma. SheerLuxe's Editor-in-Chief called it her "absolute favorite restaurant on the island." Single-source but an unambiguous superlative; the best dinner candidate for a Palma night. Manus's Sunday report ranks it the strongest food-first indoor fallback (open daily, Sunday dinner 19:00–23:30): scallop, ceviche, salmon, tuna, prawns, lobster pasta, turbot, monkfish, sea bass and vegetable dishes in the atmospheric 19th-century former bakery in La Lonja.
